headline: Controversy as PM asks Ishraque to resign, minister's office denies
summary: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman reportedly asked State Minister for Liberation War Affairs Ishraque Hossain to step down following a controversial anti-drug raid.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has reportedly ordered State Minister for Liberation War Affairs Ishraque Hossain to resign from the cabinet.
The move comes after Ishraque Hossain sparked controversy by leading an anti-drug operation while carrying a firearm.
Ishraque Hossain's office and his press secretary have dismissed the reports of a resignation order as 'baseless' and 'rumors'.
The State Minister had previously stated he would use bamboo sticks instead of firearms to destroy drug dens in the future.
The situation remains tense as conflicting reports emerge regarding the minister's status in the cabinet.
caption:
Did the Prime Minister order State Minister Ishraque Hossain to resign over a firearm controversy?

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has reportedly ordered State Minister for Liberation War Affairs Ishraque Hossain to resign from the cabinet.

The move comes after Ishraque Hossain sparked controversy by leading an anti-drug operation while carrying a firearm.

Ishraque Hossain's office and his press secretary have dismissed the reports of a resignation order as 'baseless' and 'rumors'.

The State Minister had previously stated he would use bamboo sticks instead of firearms to destroy drug dens in the future.

The situation remains tense as conflicting reports emerge regarding the minister's status in the cabinet.

Source: Dhaka Tribune, Prothom Alo, Jamuna TV

headline: ACC approves charge sheet against Saima Wazed over false CV claims
summary: The daughter of ousted PM Sheikh Hasina is accused of providing false information to secure a regional director post at the WHO.
details: The Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) has approved a charge sheet against Saima Wazed, daughter of former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, for allegedly providing false information in her CV.
The ACC investigation claims Saima falsely stated she worked as an honorary specialist or expert at Bangladesh Medical University, now known as Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujib Medical University Hospital.
The commission alleges she used this false information and abuse of power to secure the post of regional director for the WHO’s South-East Asia region, tarnishing the country's reputation.
According to the probe, Saima exerted pressure to have her CV forwarded to WHO headquarters in Geneva via the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, bypassing required official files and verification.
The case was filed on March 20, 2025, at the ACC’s Dhaka-1 integrated district office and was investigated by Deputy Director Tahasina Munabil Haque.
At the time of her application, Saima served as the chairperson of the Suchona Foundation and the National Advisory Committee on Autism and Neurodevelopmental Disorders.
caption:
Saima Wazed faces a charge sheet from the ACC for allegedly using a fake CV to land a top WHO position.

The Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) has approved a charge sheet against Saima Wazed, daughter of former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, for allegedly providing false information in her CV.

The ACC investigation claims Saima falsely stated she worked as an honorary specialist or expert at Bangladesh Medical University, now known as Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujib Medical University Hospital.

The commission alleges she used this false information and abuse of power to secure the post of regional director for the WHO’s South-East Asia region, tarnishing the country's reputation.

According to the probe, Saima exerted pressure to have her CV forwarded to WHO headquarters in Geneva via the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, bypassing required official files and verification.

The case was filed on March 20, 2025, at the ACC’s Dhaka-1 integrated district office and was investigated by Deputy Director Tahasina Munabil Haque.

At the time of her application, Saima served as the chairperson of the Suchona Foundation and the National Advisory Committee on Autism and Neurodevelopmental Disorders.
